{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** Legal (Customer-side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement
**Status:** Draft for negotiation

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The Agreement is acceptable in several important respects — the limitation of liability (Section 21), assignment and change of control (Section 24), and Vendor insurance (Section 18) each meet our preferred position in full and require no redline.

The balance of the document, however, is materially Vendor-favourable and contains three critical problems. First, **there is no indemnification section at all** — the outline skips from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all cross-reference indemnity obligations that do not exist. Second, **Section 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of Deliverables in Vendor**, leaving us only a revocable, non-transferable licence that expires with the Order Form term — we would not own the bespoke work product we pay for. Third, that same clause fails our licence-scope rule (revocable, term-limited, no Affiliate or contractor coverage).

A cluster of clauses also imposes one-sided restraints on us that sit at or beyond our walk-away line: a three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination rights (Section 2.1), a match/right-of-first-refusal obligation operating as de facto exclusivity and a reverse MFN (Section 7.2), an all-territory 24-month non-compete (Section 12.4), and a 24-month no-hire with no unsolicited-approach carve-out (Section 12.4, duplicate numbering). Several of these directly contradict Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. We have also flagged the absence of any termination-for-convenience right across a three-year term, and the absence of any transition-assistance or certified data-return obligation.

Finally, Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which is outside our accepted set and conflicts with Section 28.2 (New York County).

**Drafting note:** a number of proposed redlines below carry a `fail` verification status and require attorney review before the markup is released to Vendor. Two audit and renewal findings (Sections 22 and 8) are recorded as internal evidence only — the substance meets our preferred position, and the flags are lexical parser artefacts arising from figures being written in words rather than digits.

---

## 2. Findings Table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / Position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 19.5 (gap between §§ 19 and 21) | No indemnity provision exists despite cross-references in §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5. Insert new Section 20. **Verification: pass** |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor owns all Deliverables; Customer holds only a revocable term licence. Flip ownership to Customer via assignment. **Verification: repaired** |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000, with full carve-outs. No redline. **Verification: pass** |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Consent-free Customer assignment; asymmetric restraints on Vendor; no repricing on our change of control. No redline. **Verification: pass** |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Match/first-refusal obligation operates as de facto exclusivity; conflicts with § 12.3. Delete. **Verification: pass** |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Needs review | § 2.1 | Take-or-pay minimum surviving termination is a Customer-payable penalty. Strike take-or-pay mechanic and waiver of reduction/termination rights. **Verification: fail** |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Needs review | § 14.2 | Deliverable licence revocable, non-transferable, term-limited, no Affiliates/contractors. Targeted fixes only. **Verification: fail** |
| 8 | High | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Reverse MFN with no scope, time limit or comparison carve-outs; contradicts § 12.3. Delete. **Verification: pass** |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | Undefined scope, all territories, 24 months post-term; contradicts § 12.3. Delete. **Verification: pass** |
| 10 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review | § 12.4 (duplicate numbering) | One-way no-hire, all employees, 24 months, no unsolicited/general-advertising carve-out. Narrow to mutual solicitation-only, 12 months. **Verification: fail** |
| 11 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 2.1 (and § 9) | No convenience right across a three-year term; § 2.1 strips termination rights. Insert § 9.4 (30 days, pro-rata refund). **Verification: repaired** |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review | § 22.1 | Preferred position met in full (1x/12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site, 5% cost flip, no system access). Flag is a lexical false negative. Internal evidence only; no redline. **Verification: fail** |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Needs review | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts; outside accepted set and conflicts with § 28.2. Substitute New York. **Verification: fail** |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year USD 2M/year take-or-pay, no reduction or termination right; contradicts §§ 12.3 and 7.1. Delete in full. **Verification: repaired** |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Needs review | § 8.2 | 30-day opt-out, 12-month renewals, 60-day Vendor reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI/3%. Preferred position met; parser false negative. No redline. **Verification: fail** |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | § 10.1 | No transition assistance, data export or certified deletion obligation. Insert § 10.3. **Verification: pass** |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL, E&O, cyber (USD 5M) and workers' comp meet or exceed our ask. No redline. **Verification: pass** |
| 18 | Low | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Needs review | § 19.2 | Deliverable conformance window is 90 days (our fallback) rather than 12 months. Extend to 12 months. **Verification: fail** |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

The following findings are recorded as sitting at, approaching, or beyond our walk-away threshold. These should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading chips.

1. **No Vendor indemnity (Section 20 absent).** Absence of a Vendor indemnity is a critical deviation under the playbook. We require the inserted Section 20 covering third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, bodily injury and property damage, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct — together with the § 20.5 remedies that four other sections already assume exist.

2. **Deliverable ownership and licence scope (Section 14.2).** Vendor ownership of bespoke work product, coupled with a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence, is described as approaching and at the walk-away line for work product created for and paid for by us. We need ownership flipped, or at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, transferable licence extending to Affiliates and contractors.

3. **Take-or-pay minimum commitment (Section 2.1).** A three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year commitment with no reduction or termination right is the playbook walk-away position. Sanctioned fallback: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty; a 3-month-fee cap remains available on the penalty point.

4. **Reverse MFN (Section 7.2).** An open-ended obligation to disclose and extend better third-party terms to Vendor is the walk-away position. Fallback: defined product scope, 12-month duration, and reasonable-comparison carve-outs.

5. **Non-compete on Customer (Section 12.4).** Undefined scope, all territories and 24 months post-term exceeds the walk-away threshold on both scope and duration. Fallback: a single named product, term only, 12 months, with carve-outs.

6. **Non-solicitation / no-hire (Section 12.4, duplicate numbering).** Three separate walk-away triggers: one-way application, a no-hire (not merely non-solicit), and express negation of any unsolicited-approach or general-advertising carve-out. Fallback: mutual, solicitation-only, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from end of involvement, with a general-recruitment carve-out.

7. **Governing law and venue (Section 28.1).** Singapore law with exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is close to the walk-away position of foreign law with exclusive foreign venue. Section 28.2 already specifies New York County, so the internal conflict supports our position.

---

## 4. Next Steps

**A. Attorney review before markup release.** Six proposed redlines carry a `fail` verification status and must be reviewed and cleared before the markup goes to Vendor:

- § 2.1 (LD) — minimal deletion of the take-or-pay mechanic
- § 14.2 (LICENSE) — targeted licence fixes; note the high changed-character ratio reflects the brevity of the one-sentence grant, not any expansion of scope
- § 12.4 (NOSOLICIT) — three surgical substitutions
- § 28.1 (GOVLAW) — two-word jurisdiction swap
- § 19.2 (WARRANTY) — 90 days to 12 months
- §§ 22 and 8 (AUDIT, RENEWAL) — confirm these are closed as compliant with no redline and no counterparty comment

**B. Resolve the overlapping Section 2.1 and 14.2 findings.** Section 2.1 is the subject of three findings (LD, T4C, MINCOMMIT) proposing different edits, ranging from deletion in full to a narrower strike-and-soften plus a Section 9 proviso. Section 14.2 is the subject of two (IP and LICENSE). We should settle a single consolidated redline for each clause before circulating.

**C. Correct the numbering and cross-reference defects.** The Agreement skips Section 20 entirely, skips § 9.4, duplicates § 12.4, and includes a Section 23 heading with no operative text. Section 16.5 defers Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15, but Section 11 does not exist. Raise these with Vendor as clean-up items alongside the substantive inserts (new Section 20, new § 9.4, new § 10.3).

**D. Use Section 12.3 as leverage.** Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3 that we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment directly contradicts §§ 2.1, 7.2 and both instances of 12.4. We should present these as internal inconsistencies Vendor must resolve, which materially strengthens our deletion asks.

**E. Confirm no concessions needed on compliant items.** Sections 18, 21, 22, 24 and the renewal mechanics in Section 8 already meet our position. We should avoid reopening them and can point to them as evidence of a balanced review posture.

**F. Circulate the markup** with comments carrying the `[Playbook]` prefix, stating the preferred position and offering the sanctioned fallback where one exists.

---

*This memo is based solely on the verified findings supplied. Findings marked `needs_review` or with a `fail` verification status are not settled positions and require confirmation before reliance.*"}
